title: Queen's Gambit Traps
description: Twelve trap lines from the Queen's Gambit, Accepted and Declined, for both colours.
source: Based on the Lichess study "Queen's Gambit Traps" by opdzs

lines.name: QGA Trap 1: ...a6 loses the rook
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 a6 axb5 axb5 Rxa8 Nd7 b3
lines.idea: 5...axb5?? opens the a-file while the a8 rook has no defender. 6.Rxa8 wins a full rook, and 7.b3 breaks up the b5-c4 pawn chain.

lines.name: QGA Trap 2: Qf3 hits a8
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Qf3 Nc6 Qxc6+ Bd7 Qa6
lines.idea: 5...cxb5?? opens the long light-square diagonal. 6.Qf3 attacks a8, and after 6...Nc6 7.Qxc6+ Bd7 8.Qa6 White is a piece up.

lines.name: QGA Trap 3: Bxf7+ wins the queen
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 c5 e3 cxd4 Bxc4 dxe3 Bxf7+ Kxf7 Qxd8
lines.idea: 5...dxe3?? forgets that only the king guards the d8 queen. 6.Bxf7+ pulls the king away and 7.Qxd8 wins the queen.

lines.name: QGA Fianchetto Trap
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Qa4+ Bd7 Qb3
lines.idea: After 6.Qa4+ Bd7, the d7 bishop no longer covers b7. 7.Qb3 hits b7 and f7 together and Black can't hold both.

lines.name: Stunning Mate: Bxd1?? Bxf7#
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 c5 Nf3 Bg4 Ne5 Bxd1 Bxf7#
lines.idea: 6.Ne5! ignores the pin. If 6...Bxd1?? then 7.Bxf7# is mate: the e5 knight protects the bishop and the king has no squares.

lines.name: Stunning Mate: 6...Be6 line
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 c5 Nf3 Bg4 Ne5 Be6 Qa4+ Nbd7 Bxe6 fxe6 O-O
lines.idea: 6...Be6 is Black's best try. 7.Qa4+ Nbd7 8.Bxe6 fxe6 9.O-O leaves Black with broken pawns and an exposed king.

lines.name: QGD Rubinstein Trap: 12...cxd5
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Bd3 c6 Qc2 Nbd7 Nf3 Re8 O-O h6 Bf4 Nh5 Nxd5 cxd5 Bc7 Qxc7 Qxc7
lines.idea: 11...Nh5 takes a defender off d5. 12.Nxd5! cxd5?? 13.Bc7 traps the queen, and Black has to give it up for a bishop.

lines.name: QGD Rubinstein Trap: 12...Nxf4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Bd3 c6 Qc2 Nbd7 Nf3 Re8 O-O h6 Bf4 Nh5 Nxd5 Nxf4 Nxf4
lines.idea: 12...Nxf4 is Black's best answer to 12.Nxd5, but after 13.Nxf4 White is simply a pawn up.

lines.name: QGD Elephant Trap: 9.Qxb4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxd5 Bxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Kxd8 Qxb4 Nxb4 O-O-O Nxa2+
lines.idea: 6.Nxd5?? falls for the Elephant Trap. 6...Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Kxd8 wins a piece, and after 9.Qxb4 Nxb4 10.O-O-O Nxa2+ Black also grabs a pawn.

lines.name: QGD Elephant Trap: 9.e4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxd5 Bxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Kxd8 e4 Re8 Bd3 Nf4 Kd1 Bxd2 Kxd2 Nxd3 Kxd3
lines.idea: 9.e4 tries to save material, but 9...Re8 10.Bd3 Nf4 11.Kd1 Bxd2 12.Kxd2 Nxd3 13.Kxd3 still leaves Black a piece up.

lines.name: QGD Cambridge Springs Trap
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3 c6 e3 Qa5 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 Ne4
lines.idea: 6...Qa5 pins the c3 knight. After 7.Bd3? dxc4 8.Bxc4 Ne4 Black hits the pinned knight and the g5 bishop, and White loses a piece.

lines.name: Albin Countergambit: Lasker Trap
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+ Rxg1 Bg4+
lines.idea: 6.Bxb4?? exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+! promotes to a knight with check, then 8.Rxg1 Bg4+ skewers the king and wins White's queen.

explain.|d4: Every line here starts by taking the centre with the queen's pawn two squares.
explain.d4 d5|c4: Offer the c-pawn now. The Queen's Gambit tempts Black to give up the centre by taking it.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4|e3: Black grabbed c4. Open the diagonal for your f1 bishop so it can win that pawn back.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4|Nf3: In this line, develop the king's knight first. It keeps d4 protected and stops ...e5 before you go after the c4 pawn.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4|*: Black grabbed c4. Prepare to win it back with a developing move: either open the f1 bishop's diagonal or bring out the king's knight.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5|a4: Black is propping up c4 with ...b5. Attack that b5 pawn from the side with your a-pawn to break the chain.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 a6|axb5: Capture on b5. If Black recaptures with the a-pawn, the a-file opens straight to the rook on a8.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 a6 axb5 axb5|Rxa8: The a-file is open and the a8 rook has no defender. Check what your a1 rook can capture.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 a6 axb5 axb5 Rxa8: You are a whole rook up. Now break the b5-c4 pawn chain by attacking c4 with your b-pawn.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6|axb5: Capture on b5. If Black recaptures with the c-pawn, the long light-square diagonal to a8 opens.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5|Qf3: Black's c-pawn left c6, so the long diagonal runs straight to the a8 rook. Find a queen move that attacks it.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Qf3: The c6 knight is only a blocker and nothing defends it properly. Take it, with check.
You are a piece up and your queen is attacked. Retreat it to a safe square on the queenside where it stays active.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 c5|e3: Black is hitting d4. Support the centre and open the f1 bishop's diagonal toward c4.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 c5 e3 cxd4|Bxc4: Don't recapture on d4 yet. Win back the c4 pawn while developing, with your bishop aiming at f7.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 c5 e3 cxd4 Bxc4 dxe3|B: Black's queen on d8 faces yours on the open d-file and only the king guards it. Lure the king away with a sacrifice that gives check.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 c5 e3 cxd4 Bxc4 dxe3 B: The king left d8 undefended. Take the queen.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6|Bxc4: Win back the gambit pawn on c4 with your bishop right now.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 g6|Nf3: Develop the king's knight and get ready to castle.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 g6 Nf3 Bg7|Qa4: Black's queenside is loose: b7 and the c8 bishop are not well covered. Give a queen check that sets up a double attack next move.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Qa4: The bishop on d7 no longer guards b7. Find the queen square that hits b7 and f7 at the same time.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 c5|Nf3: Protect d4 and develop. The knight also prepares to castle.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 c5 Nf3 Bg4|Ne5: Don't worry about the pin. Jump the knight forward: it attacks the g4 bishop and, with your c4 bishop, targets f7.
explain.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 c5 Nf3 Bg4 Ne5: Black took your queen, but f7 is fatal. Your bishop lands there backed by the e5 knight and the king has no squares.
Give check with the queen. It pressures the a4-e8 diagonal and keeps the initiative.
Trade on e6. After ...fxe6 Black's pawns are damaged and the king is exposed.
Get your king safe before doing anything else.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6|Nc3: Black declined the gambit. Develop the queen's knight to add pressure on d5.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6|cxd5: Release the tension with the Exchange Variation: take on d5 to fix Black's pawn structure.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5|Bg5: Develop the dark-squared bishop and pin the f6 knight.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5 Bg5 Be7|e3: Open the f1 bishop's diagonal and support d4.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5 Bg5 Be7 e3: Develop the light-squared bishop toward Black's kingside.
Line up the queen behind the d3 bishop on the b1-h7 diagonal.
Develop the king's knight before castling.
The g5 bishop is attacked. Retreat it to a square where it stays on an active diagonal.
The knight left f6, so d5 has lost a defender. Grab it. If ...cxd5, your f4 bishop can trap Black's queen.
Black's queen on d8 has no safe squares. Attack it with the bishop.
Take the piece back. You come out a clean pawn up.
explain.d4|d5: Meet 1.d4 by claiming the centre with your own queen's pawn.
explain.d4 d5 c4|e6: Decline the gambit solidly: support d5 with a pawn and open your f8 bishop.
explain.d4 d5 c4|e5: Counter-gambit: hit back in the centre with your e-pawn instead of defending d5.
explain.d4 d5 c4|*: Two answers are in this course: support d5 solidly with a pawn, or counter-attack in the centre with your e-pawn.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3|Nf6: Develop the king's knight to defend d5.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5|Nbd7: Develop the queen's knight. It looks like it blocks your bishop, but it sets the Elephant Trap.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5|exd5: Recapture on d5 with the e-pawn.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5 exd5 N: White's knight grabbed d5. Take it. Your queen looks hanging, but you have a check coming.
White took your queen. Check the king with your dark-squared bishop and you will win the queen back.
Recapture White's bishop on d8. You end up a piece ahead.
Take White's queen with the d5 knight.
Your bishop pins White's queen to the king. Bring a rook to the e-file to add pressure on e4 and the king.
Your d5 knight is attacked. Move it to a square that hits the d3 bishop and g2.
Trade off the d3 bishop with your knight.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3|c6: Strengthen d5 with your c-pawn. This also opens the a5-e1 diagonal for your queen.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3 c6 e3|Q: Pin the c3 knight with your queen. The g5 bishop also loses its support.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3 c6 e3 Q: Take on c4 to pull White's bishop away from d3.
Hit the pinned c3 knight and the g5 bishop at once. White can't hold both.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5|d4: Push your d-pawn forward to gain space and cramp White.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3|Bb4+: Give a bishop check before taking on e3.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2|dxe3: Now take on e3, hitting f2 and d2.
explain.d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb: Promote on g1, but pick the piece that gives check. A queen here would not.
Check the king along the diagonal and skewer White's queen on d1.
